pending_qa.q: What are the financial consequences of choosing a 30-year mortgage versus a 15-year mortgage for first-time homebuyers?
pending_qa.r: The rates are significantly higher on a 30-year mortgage compared to a 15-year mortgage. Over 30 years, the total amount paid would be substantially more, and most homeowners do not stay in the same house for 30 years anyway.

pending_qa.q: How can couples identify and address hidden spending patterns when combined household income exceeds expenses?
pending_qa.r: Pull credit reports from annualcreditreport.com to see all open accounts and debts, and have an honest conversation about where money is actually going. Lee and his wife making $225,000 combined annually cannot account for tens of thousands of dollars, indicating either undisclosed spending, separate financial accounts without transparency, or potentially more serious marital issues.

pending_qa.q: What housing affordability threshold should guide first-time homebuyers with limited down payments?
pending_qa.r: Justin indicated he wanted to stay under about $200,000 for a house purchase, and was considering a 30-year mortgage to make payments more affordable. The hosts advised that securing stable employment at a higher income level should come before committing to any mortgage.

pending_qa.q: How should a homebuyer evaluate selling a primary residence to pay off student loan debt?
pending_qa.r: Patrick sold his home of 10 years that he purchased for $80,000 at 3% interest to pay off student loans after filing bankruptcy in 2012. He subsequently rented for 3-4 years at $2,400 per month before buying another house for $230,000 with no money down at 6.25% interest, a decision he later regretted.
